title: Stoicism again with Priya
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). A week later, Alex and Priya apply Marcus Aurelius and Epictetus to waiting for the studio's answer, contrast Stoicism with mindfulness and Buddhist non-attachment, detour into the Small Hours podcast, then return to Stoicism.

utterances.text: So? Did the studio call?
No. They said Monday, then they emailed that it'll be the end of the week. I'm losing my mind a bit.
Okay, Stoicism round two. What's up to you right now?
Nothing! I countered, I answered their questions. Now it's just waiting.
Then that's the point. Epictetus would say the decision is theirs, your reaction is yours.
I know. I even reread Marcus Aurelius this week for book club. The morning reminder thing. It helps for like an hour.
Can I push on something, though? Lately I've been using a meditation app, and it's honestly a different approach.
Isn't mindfulness basically Stoicism with a nicer voice?
People mix them up, but no. Stoicism uses reason. You sort things into in my control and not in my control, and you argue with your own judgments.
Right, the Epictetus thing. It's our judgments that upset us.
Mindfulness doesn't argue. You just notice the thought, oh, there's anxiety about the job, and you let it pass without fixing it.
Huh. So no list, no sorting.
And the Buddhist idea behind it is non-attachment. The suffering comes from clinging, to outcomes, even to the self.
But the Stoics still care a lot. Marcus wants to do his duty, be a good emperor.
Exactly. Stoicism says care about your own character, let go of the rest. Non-attachment says loosen your grip on all of it, even the wanting.
Okay, that's a real difference. One sorts, one lets go.
I think I need both. Oh, speaking of letting go, did you hear the new Small Hours?
Not yet! Is the camel guy back?
No, it's a woman who sailed alone for a month and talked to a seagull the whole time.
Ha, that show is just people befriending animals in remote places.
It's the whole brand. Anyway, sorry, back to your Stoic crisis.
Yeah. So if I do the Stoic thing properly, what do I actually do this week?
Write down what's yours. Your current work, your run on Saturday, calling your mom. Do those well.
And the studio goes on the other list.
And if they say no, Marcus would say that's material to work with, not a disaster.
The obstacle becomes the way.
Look at you, quoting emperors.
Okay. I'll try the sorting this week, and maybe your app for the four a.m. part.
That's a pretty good combination, honestly.
